newsitem.title: UK: British retail sales rise in line with forecasts.
newsitem.headline: British retail sales rise in line with forecasts.

text.p: British retail sales rose by 0.4 percent in October compared with a fall of 0.3 percent the previous month, the Office for National Statistics said on Wednesday.
Retail sales rose by an annual rate of 4.1 percent in October against a 3.6 percent rise the previous month. The figures were broadly in line with market forecasts.
The Treasury said the rise in retail sales showed increased confidence among British consumers.
"Rising high street sales show that people have the cash to spend and the confidence to do it," Economic Secretary to the Treasury Angela Knight said.
Government bonds, which had fallen overnight, rose slightly on the retail sales news, but leading shares generally eased.
Britain raised interest rates three weeks ago in an attempt to head off risks of a rise in inflation.
